note: The site's own words for each checked item, written to the site's rules. An item is shown only if verified_<case>.json confirmed or corrected it, it has a sentence here, and it is not in drop. group is records (the Commission's or an officer's own table or order), reported (press), or said (what a party or an official said, as reported).

cases.title: Kichha, Uttarakhand
cases.intro: Kichha is the assembly constituency in Udham Singh Nagar, a plains district on the border with Uttar Pradesh, that lost the largest share of its roll in Uttarakhand.

drop.kichha-16: The court-ordered FIR is in Haldwani, Nainital district, and does not concern Kichha.

kichha-01: The Chief Electoral Officer's table of the draft of 14 July 2026 gives Kichha a draft of 1,21,545 electors and 27,068 names left off. The same row counts 36,937 electors on the draft with an anomaly and 9,810 with no mapping to the last intensive revision, which together put them in line for a notice. It gives no reason for any name left off.
kichha-14: The Chief Electoral Officer's table of the final roll (PN 63/2026, 3 October 2026) shows 1,503 claims and 4,439 objections admitted in Kichha after the draft. That is 36.5 names deleted for every 1,000 on the draft, against 14.7 in the state. Women were 2,186 of the 4,439.
kichha-02: Amar Ujala reported on 15 July 2026 that Udham Singh Nagar's draft held 11,55,672 electors and that its share of forms not collected, 13.33 per cent, was the highest of any district in the state, against 10.39 per cent for the state.
kichha-03: The Indian Express, reading the Chief Electoral Officer's presentation to parties of 3 October 2026, reported 1,77,673 names left off in Udham Singh Nagar, the second most of any district after Dehradun.
kichha-12: The Indian Express reported on 10 September 2026 that Udham Singh Nagar accounted for 43,878 of Uttarakhand's 1,30,382 Form 7 applications to delete a name, the most of any district, with 34,903 still being processed on 7 September.
kichha-06: The Times of India reported on 29 August 2026 nearly 9,300 objections in Kichha, 1,707 on the ground that the elector had shifted for good and 7,589 alleging the elector was enrolled twice. It reported that 6,412 of the second kind were filed by one booth-level agent of the BJP.
kichha-13: Hindustan Times reported on 25 September 2026 the Chief Electoral Officer's statement that about 95,000 of roughly 1.73 lakh Form 7 applications in Uttarakhand were generated by the system when electors with a notice were marked ineligible after failing or missing their hearing.
kichha-05: Kichha's Electoral Registration Officer told Newslaundry that the portal had accepted the bulk submissions, that the rules require a check when one person files many, and that no name would be deleted without a field check, a notice and a hearing.
kichha-11: The Kumaon Commissioner told The Times of India that no name would be deleted without verification, a notice and a chance for the elector to give evidence.
kichha-07: The Congress told the Election Commission in a memorandum of 20 August 2026, as The Hindu reported, that one man had filed 6,410 objections in Kichha and that 262 people in Uttarakhand had each filed more than ten Form 7s.
kichha-08: Kichha's Congress MLA alleged, as Dainik Bhaskar reported on 5 August 2026, that Form 7 objections were filed online in residents' names without their knowledge, with 90 to 95 in one name within three days. He gave the data to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate and asked for an FIR.
kichha-09: A BJP spokesperson who is a former Kichha MLA said, as The Times of India reported, that the party's own review found more than 8,000 electors on Kichha's roll also registered in Bareilly, Pilibhit and Rampur in Uttar Pradesh. No official figure for this was found.

not_found: Any statement by Kichha's Electoral Registration Officer or Udham Singh Nagar's District Election Officer on why Kichha lost the largest share of its roll, and any split of its names left off by reason.
Any count for Kichha of booth-level officers, notices issued, hearings held or electors marked ineligible after a hearing.
An official count of Form 7 applications in Kichha. The press counts differ, and the final-roll table gives only the 4,439 objections admitted.
Any FIR registered in Udham Singh Nagar over Form 7s filed in other people's names, and any court case about Kichha.
Any documented account of what in Kichha itself, such as work, housing or evictions, lies behind its figure. Only the parties' explanations were found.

cases.title: Tughlakabad, Delhi
cases.intro: Tughlakabad is the assembly constituency in Delhi's South East district that lost the largest share of its roll of the city's 70.

drop.tughlakabad-09: A single elector's story, from a profile that identifies him. The site publishes counts only.

tughlakabad-01: The Chief Electoral Officer's table of 31 August 2026 gives Tughlakabad a draft of 1,00,386 electors and 92,033 enumeration forms not collected, 47.8 of every 100 on the roll before the revision, the most of any of Delhi's 70 seats.
tughlakabad-11: The AAP won Tughlakabad in the 2025 Assembly election by 14,711 votes, so the names left off are more than six times the winning margin. That makes them large enough to decide the seat, which says nothing about whether they would have.
tughlakabad-12: The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office posted that special camps for all electors were held in Tughlakabad during the revision. The post gives no date and no count.
tughlakabad-04: Hindustan Times reported on 18 August 2026, from the Chief Electoral Officer's data, that when enumeration closed on 17 August only 52.14 per cent of Tughlakabad's forms had been entered, the lowest in Delhi, and that South East was the lowest district at 56.32 per cent.
tughlakabad-02: NDTV reported on 2 September 2026, citing the Election Commission's data, the same 92,033 forms not collected in Tughlakabad, followed by Okhla at 45.16 per cent.
tughlakabad-03: The Times of India reported on 1 September 2026 that South East was the district with the most forms not collected, 43.6 per cent (6,79,081 of 15,57,289).
tughlakabad-05: NDTV India reported on 18 August 2026 that Tughlakabad is home to migrant workers employed along the Faridabad border, and that experts it did not name linked the low return of forms in Tughlakabad and Okhla to this.
tughlakabad-06: In an NDTV India report from Gola Kuan and Bengali Colony on 18 August 2026, residents said workers who commute to Faridabad, Noida and Gurgaon were marked as shifted though they live there, and that tenants could not show papers such as electricity bills.
tughlakabad-10: Before enumeration began, Delhi's Chief Electoral Officer told The Indian Express on 30 June 2026 that electors whose houses had been demolished would not be found at their address, that their forms could not be collected, so they would not be on the draft, and that such cases would be dealt with separately and taken to the Election Commission. The statement was about Delhi as a whole.

not_found: Any statement by Tughlakabad's Electoral Registration Officer or South East's District Election Officer on the seat's figure, and any split of its names left off by reason from the Chief Electoral Officer.
Any count for Tughlakabad of booth-level officers, notices, hearings, or Form 6 and Form 7 applications after the draft. Delhi's final roll is due on 4 December 2026.
Any court case, party complaint or protest about Tughlakabad alone, and any statement by its MLA.
Any documented link between the seat's figure and a particular demolition or eviction.

cases.title: Danilimda, Gujarat
cases.intro: Danilimda is an Ahmedabad constituency reserved for Scheduled Castes, around Chandola Lake, where the city demolished thousands of homes in 2025. It is the one Ahmedabad seat whose final roll is smaller than its draft.

drop.dan-07: No source places the Isanpur lake demolition in Danilimda.
drop.dan-10: The petitions concern Kodinar and Sidhpur, not Danilimda.

dan-03: The Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation demolished more than 10,000 structures around Chandola Lake, in Danilimda, on 29 April and 20 May 2025, months before the revision began, as The Quint reported.
dan-01: Gujarat Samachar reported on 8 February 2026 that 634 Form 7 applications to delete names were filed in two of Danilimda's polling booths, 193 and 194, by two people it described as BJP workers, and that a complaint was registered at Isanpur police station. No outcome of the complaint was found.
dan-02: The same report described a dispute over applications to delete the names of residents left homeless by the Chandola Lake demolitions, which alleged that their lack of papers for an address was being used to seek their deletion.
dan-06: A rights group's letter to Gujarat's Chief Electoral Officer of 17 January 2026, reported by Counterview, said residents moved from Chandola Lake were given special camps to complete their forms and that their names are on the draft. No official confirmation of the camps was found.
dan-04: Bhaskar English reported on 3 October 2026 that the municipal ward of Danilimda, which takes in the Chandola Lake area, had 19,346 fewer voters on the city's rolls in 2026 than in 2021. The paper said the fall does not show by itself how many names the revision left off or deleted. The ward is smaller than the assembly constituency.
dan-08: BBC News Gujarati reported on 21 February 2026 that some organisations said the names and reasons of electors deleted between the draft and the final roll of 17 February had not been published, though such lists were available at the draft.
dan-09: The Hindu reported that Gujarat's election officials gave two very different counts of Form 7 applications in the state two days apart, 9,88,621 on 29 January and 1,83,235 on 31 January 2026, and that the Chief Electoral Officer did not answer its question about the gap.
dan-05: The Congress's Ahmedabad unit told Bhaskar English that many demolition drives were aimed at particular constituencies and wards, and that it had worked on voter deletions over the past year.

not_found: Any statement, release or table from Gujarat's Chief Electoral Officer or Ahmedabad's District Election Officer about Danilimda alone, including counts of Form 6 and Form 7 applications, notices and hearings.
Any reason for the 8,289 names deleted from Danilimda's roll after the draft, or for its final roll being the one in Ahmedabad smaller than its draft.
Any outcome of the police complaint over the 634 Form 7s, or any decision by the Electoral Registration Officer on them.
Any court case or documented protest about Danilimda alone.

cases.title: Murshidabad, Malda and the Dinajpurs, West Bengal
cases.intro: Murshidabad and Malda are the West Bengal districts with the most names sent to judicial officers for adjudication after the draft, close to a third of the state's. The Commission's district table, as the press printed it, sets Uttar and Dakshin Dinajpur beside them, and of the four Dakshin Dinajpur had the largest share found not eligible.

mm-07: On 2 April 2026 the Supreme Court took up on its own the surrounding of seven judicial officers at the Block Development Office in Kaliachak, Malda (Suo Motu W.P.(C) 3 of 2026). It ordered central forces wherever judicial officers were deciding revision cases, asked Malda's District Magistrate and Superintendent of Police to explain themselves, and directed that the inquiry be handed to the CBI or the NIA.
mm-02: The Election Commission's district table of adjudication outcomes, as The Indian Express printed it on 7 April 2026, gives Murshidabad 11,01,145 cases, of whom 6,33,671 were found eligible and 4,55,137 not. Malda had 8,28,127 cases, 5,88,657 and 2,39,375. Uttar Dinajpur had 4,80,341, 3,03,261 and 1,76,972. Dakshin Dinajpur had 1,32,258, 55,490 and 76,768.
mm-01: The Hindu reported that of the 60,06,675 cases under adjudication when the final roll was published on 28 February 2026, about 11 lakh were in Murshidabad and about 8 lakh in Malda, close to a third of the state's, with 4.8 lakh in Uttar Dinajpur.
mm-03: Hindustan Times reported on 8 April 2026, from the Commission's data, that Murshidabad had the most names deleted after adjudication of any district and Malda the third most, and that 58.1 per cent of Dakshin Dinajpur's cases were found not eligible.
mm-04: The Times of India reported on 10 April 2026, from the Commission's data, that Samserganj in Murshidabad lost 74,775 of its 1,08,400 names under adjudication and Lalgola 55,420 of 99,082, and that more than 37,000 of 79,683 under adjudication in Mothabari, Malda, were deleted.
mm-05: The Indian Express reported on 29 March 2026 booth counts of names under adjudication that were deleted, 327 of 444 and 422 of 527 in two booths of a village in Sujapur, Malda, and 291 of 591 and 207 of 361 in booths 111 and 112 of Suti, Murshidabad.
mm-06: The New Indian Express reported that on 1 April 2026 electors deleted after adjudication surrounded seven judicial officers at the Block Development Office in Kaliachak, Malda, and blocked National Highway 12. It put Malda's adjudicated electors at about 8.30 lakh, against a district roll of 29.86 lakh.
mm-08: The Economic Times reported, from PTI, that the NIA, which took over the Mothabari case on the Supreme Court's direction, had arrested 68 people by 26 May 2026.
mm-11: SabrangIndia reported on 13 October 2026 The Wire's reading of the Commission's own figures filed with the Supreme Court. In Murshidabad, by that reading, 10.58 per cent of Form 6 applications led to a name being added, against 87.71 per cent of Form 7 requests leading to a name being deleted. In Uttar Dinajpur it was 8.16 against 96.11 per cent. The site has not read the affidavit itself.
mm-09: On a visit to Beldanga in Murshidabad, West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer told an elector asking for deleted names to be restored that the deletions had been made by judicial officers under the Supreme Court's directions, as The New Indian Express reported on 12 April 2026. The paper put what it called Murshidabad's deletions at 7,48,959.

not_found: Any release from the District Election Officers of Murshidabad or Malda with their own counts of adjudication, Form 6, Form 7 or hearings.
The Commission's own copy of its district table of adjudication outcomes. Only newspapers' copies were found.
Any official count, by district or constituency, of appeals decided, or of names restored after an appeal.
The reasons for adjudication outcomes by district.
Any Calcutta High Court order on adjudication in these districts.

cases.title: Bhiwandi East, Maharashtra
cases.intro: Bhiwandi East is an assembly constituency in Thane district. It had the largest share of its roll left off the draft of any of Maharashtra's 288 seats.

bhe-01: The statement the Chief Electoral Officer enclosed with the press note of 16 September 2026 lists Bhiwandi East first of the state's 288 seats, with 3,76,138 electors before the revision and 1,84,692 enumeration forms not collected, 49.10 per cent.
bhe-02: The Chief Electoral Officer's tables of 1 September 2026 give the reasons entered for Bhiwandi East's 1,84,692 names. 86,256 were marked untraceable or absent, 68,255 permanently shifted, 15,662 already enrolled elsewhere, 8,744 dead and 5,775 other. Shifted and absent together are 83.7 per cent of the total, and the dead are 4.7 per cent. Each reason is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.
bhe-03: The same tables give Bhiwandi East a draft roll of 1,91,446 electors, 1,00,418 men, 90,968 women and 60 third gender. Women are 47.5 per cent of the draft. The Chief Electoral Officer has published no split by sex of the names left off.
bhe-04: The Samajwadi Party won Bhiwandi East in the 2024 Assembly election by 52,015 votes over the Shiv Sena, on a roll of 3,73,659, according to the Election Commission's results. The 1,84,692 names left off the draft are 3.6 times that margin. That makes them large enough to decide the seat, which says nothing about whether they would have.
bhe-09: In its press note of 16 September 2026 the Chief Electoral Officer said that electors in the shifted, absent or other categories could apply on Form 6 to be included during the claims period, then running from 31 August to 30 September 2026. The note said the high share of forms not collected appears in urban seats because electors keep moving from one place to another. The explanation is for the state as a whole and does not name Bhiwandi East. The claims period was later extended to 12 October 2026.
bhe-05: The Free Press Journal reported on 10 August 2026, before the draft, that 48.20 per cent of Bhiwandi East's roll had been digitised, the least of the three Bhiwandi seats. Officials the paper did not name said many migrant workers who lived in Bhiwandi in 2002 had since gone back to their villages or moved to other cities.
bhe-06: The same report quoted a booth-level officer in Bhiwandi East, who was not named, saying that tenants had moved without leaving word of where they went and that people in their buildings were reluctant to sign forms for those who no longer lived there. The paper itself reported that some workers were listed both in their home villages and in Bhiwandi.
bhe-07: The Times of India reported on 23 August 2026 that Bhiwandi East had the highest share of forms not collected in the state, 49.1 per cent, against 6.11 per cent in Akole, the lowest. Officials told the paper that a form not collected did not by itself take away anyone's vote.
bhe-08: The Hindu reported on 15 September 2026, from the Commission's figures, that Bhiwandi East had the highest share in Maharashtra, 49.1 per cent or 1.85 lakh of 3.76 lakh names, which the paper called deletions. In the same article the paper wrote that 'permanently shifted' and 'untraceable or absent' seemed to have been used as blanket categories across the state. It illustrated that reading with other seats and made no such finding about Bhiwandi East.
bhe-10: On 1 September 2026, the day after the draft, Bhiwandi East's Samajwadi Party MLA posted that over 50 per cent of names had been cut in the constituency, that 27,000 of the remaining electors showed discrepancies and 17,000 had no link to old records, and asked electors to file Form 6 through booth-level officers or the party's booth agents. These are the MLA's figures and they are unconfirmed. The Chief Electoral Officer's figures are 49.10 per cent left off and a draft of 1,91,446, and no official table found gives notices by seat. No reply from the Commission was found.
bhe-11: A Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA said in a presentation on the rolls, as The Indian Express reported on 10 October 2026, that 1,91,691 votes were cast in Bhiwandi East in 2024 while its draft roll held 1,91,446, fewer than the number who voted. Comparing votes cast with a draft roll is the party's comparison. Election Commission officials replied that differences between the counts before the revision and the draft came from removing duplicate registrations and that the lists had been published. Their reply was about Maharashtra as a whole and did not address Bhiwandi East.

not_found: Any statement by Bhiwandi East's Electoral Registration Officer or Thane's District Election Officer on why the seat had the state's largest share left off. The only official explanation found is the Chief Electoral Officer's, which covers the whole state.

Any official count for Bhiwandi East of notices, hearings, or Form 6 and Form 7 applications. The Chief Electoral Officer published notices by district only, and no published table carries the MLA's figures of 27,000 and 17,000.
Any figures for Bhiwandi East by polling station or ward. The Chief Electoral Officer's table gives the seat's total only.
Any court case, FIR or protest about the revision in Bhiwandi East alone.
The text of the MLA's posts on Facebook and Instagram.
Anything after the draft. Maharashtra's final roll is due on 16 November 2026.

cases.title: Anna Nagar, Tamil Nadu
cases.intro: Anna Nagar is an assembly constituency in Chennai district. It had the largest share of its roll left off the draft of any of Tamil Nadu's 234 seats.

an-01: The Chief Electoral Officer's table of names left off the draft of 19 December 2025 gives Anna Nagar 1,18,287. Of these 1,08,829 were marked shifted or absent, which the table counts together, 8,819 dead and 639 enrolled at more than one place. Shifted or absent are 92 per cent of the total. Each reason is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.
an-02: The Chief Electoral Officer's draft roll of 19 December 2025 gave Anna Nagar 1,62,135 electors, 78,287 men, 83,802 women and 46 third gender. The final roll of 23 February 2026 gave 1,81,402, with 87,325 men, 94,029 women and 48 third gender. That is a net rise of 19,267, which counts new voters as well as anyone put back.
an-03: Anna Nagar went to the 2026 Assembly election on a roll of 1,88,861. The TVK won by 21,363 votes over the DMK, which had won the seat in 2021 by 27,445, according to the Election Commission's results. The 1,18,287 names left off the draft are 5.5 times the 2026 margin. That makes them large enough to decide the seat, which says nothing about whether they would have.
an-04: The Hindu reported on 20 December 2025, from a press release of the Greater Chennai Corporation, which runs the elections in the city, that Anna Nagar had the highest share left off of Chennai's 16 seats, 42.18 per cent, and Dr. Radhakrishnan Nagar the lowest, 24.19 per cent.
an-07: Anna Nagar Times, a neighbourhood weekly, reported in its issue of 7 December 2025, before the draft, that help desks the Corporation set up at polling booths across the city until 25 November helped voters who had not received a form when booth-level officers went door to door, and that the officers had resumed home visits to collect forms. The report was about the whole city.
an-08: The Hindu reported on 12 October 2026, citing the Chennai District Election Office, that Anna Nagar had the fewest Form 6 applications for inclusion of Chennai's 16 seats in the special drive of 10 and 11 October 2026, after the revision and the election, with 48.
an-05: The Greater Chennai Corporation's commissioner, who is Chennai's District Election Officer, told The Times of India on 19 December 2025 that the city's exclusions came from heavy migration and people changing house, including within the city, and that people who had moved could enrol again on Form 6. The explanation was for the whole district.
an-06: At the release of Chennai's draft, as The Times of India reported on 19 December 2025, the AIADMK said a single family had been split across four booths. The DMK said 14 lakh names had gone with no explanation of how 12 lakh had shifted, and the BJP asked how electors left off the draft could sign Form 6's declaration that they hold no voter card. The commissioner told the BJP he would check the point with the Election Commission. All three statements were about Chennai district as a whole.

not_found: Any statement by Anna Nagar's Electoral Registration Officer on why the seat had the largest share left off in Tamil Nadu. Only the district's explanation was found.
Any count for Anna Nagar of notices to electors not found in the 2005 roll, hearings held or names deleted after a hearing. Only Chennai's total of 2,37,619 electors due a notice was found.
Any count for Anna Nagar of Form 6 or Form 7 applications in the claims period after the draft. The net rise to the final roll is the only measure.
Any official figures for Anna Nagar by polling station.
Any court case, FIR or protest about the revision in Anna Nagar alone.
Any statement about the names left off by the candidates in Anna Nagar in 2021 or 2026.
The text of Tamil television reports naming Anna Nagar that were posted on Facebook.

cases.title: Lucknow district, Uttar Pradesh
cases.intro: Lucknow is the district of Uttar Pradesh's capital, with nine assembly seats. It had the largest share of its roll left off the draft of any of the state's 75 districts.

lko-01: The Chief Electoral Officer's district table of the draft of 6 January 2026, as photographed and published by India TV, gives Lucknow 39,94,535 electors before the revision, 27,94,397 on the draft and 12,00,138 left off. Of these 5,35,855 were marked permanently shifted, 4,27,705 untraceable or absent, 1,28,242 dead, 49,046 already enrolled elsewhere and 59,290 other. Each reason is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.
lko-07: The Lucknow district administration publishes the lists of electors whose enumeration forms were not collected for each of the nine assembly seats, and a page for the final roll of 10 April 2026 that links lists for three of them. The lists carry electors' names, and the site does not use them.
lko-03: The Indian Express reported on 28 December 2025, from officials, that Lucknow had more electors marked untraceable (4.27 lakh) and more marked shifted (5.35 lakh) than any other district in the state. An official the paper did not name said absentees were higher in urban areas because the addresses and personal details on the rolls were least accurate there.
lko-08: Dainik Bhaskar reported on 6 January 2026 that Lucknow North fell from 4.99 lakh electors to 3.07 lakh at the draft and Sarojininagar from 6.02 lakh to 4.12 lakh, and Lucknow Cantonment from 3.65 lakh to 2.22 lakh. The paper wrote that officials and election analysts, whom it did not name, put the fall down to jobs, study, transfers and migration within cities.
lko-02: Hindustan Times reported on 7 January 2026, from data it said the District Magistrate made available, the share left off the draft in each of the nine seats. It was 39.11 per cent in Lucknow Cantonment, 38.39 in Lucknow North, 36.77 in Lucknow East, 34.61 in Lucknow Central, 31.42 in Sarojininagar, 30.25 in Lucknow West, 22.27 in Bakshi Ka Talab, 17.41 in Malihabad and 16.93 in Mohanlalganj. The counts the paper printed beside three of these seats contain slips. Worked back from the district totals, Lucknow Cantonment went from 3,65,590 electors to 2,22,598, which gives the paper's 39.11 per cent and agrees with Dainik Bhaskar. These are press figures, and no official table by seat was found.
lko-06: The Times of India reported on 18 April 2026, in its own analysis of the revision's figures, a fall of 34.18 per cent in Lucknow Cantonment, over 1.24 lakh names and the highest rate in the state, and of 28.88 per cent in Lucknow Central, 1.07 lakh. Both are larger than the seats' 2022 winning margins of 39,512 and 10,935. The paper does not say where its seat figures come from or which roll they run to. They are lower than the falls at the draft, so they appear to be net falls to the final roll, which count new voters too.
lko-05: ThePrint reported on 28 August 2026 that on the final roll, published in April 2026, Lucknow again had the largest fall in Uttar Pradesh from the roll before the revision, 9.14 lakh or 22.89 per cent, which the paper called deletions. It is a net fall that counts names added after the draft as well as names deleted. No official district table of the final roll was found to check it.
lko-04: An Additional District Magistrate in Lucknow told Hindustan Times on 31 January 2026 that notices had been generated for 3,98,749 of the district's 4.78 lakh electors with no mapping to the old roll and that hearings had been completed for 45,000. The officer said 171 Electoral Registration Officers and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers were holding hearings every day, and that an elector living elsewhere could send a family member or acquaintance with an authorisation letter and documents.

not_found: Any official table of Lucknow's final roll by seat or by reason. The 9.14 lakh fall to the final roll is a press figure.
Any official table of Lucknow's draft by assembly seat. Every seat figure here comes from the press.
Any official count for Lucknow district of Form 6 and Form 7 applications, or of names deleted after a hearing.
Any split by sex of the names left off in Lucknow. The figures by sex in the press are for the state only.
Any statement by the District Election Officer on why Lucknow had the state's largest share left off. The only explanation found is an unnamed official's general remark about urban rolls.
Any party complaint about Lucknow district's figures in particular.
Any court case, FIR or protest about the revision in Lucknow district alone.

cases.title: B.B.M.P (South), Bengaluru, Karnataka
cases.intro: B.B.M.P (South) is one of the election districts of Bengaluru, with seven assembly seats from Govindarajanagar to Bommanahalli. It had the largest share of its roll left off the draft of Karnataka's 34 election districts.

bbs-01: The Chief Electoral Officer's press note of 24 August 2026 gives B.B.M.P (South) 21,44,784 electors before the revision and 10,58,028 left off the draft. Of these 6,19,986 were marked shifted, 2,66,552 absent, 69,448 dead, 10,939 already enrolled elsewhere and 91,103 other. Shifted is 58.6 per cent of the total, and 10,86,756 forms were digitised. Each reason is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.
bbs-02: The Chief Electoral Officer's press note of 9 October 2026 gives B.B.M.P (South) 4,18,213 notices generated, 4,17,945 delivered and 268 not delivered. It counts 3,52,610 hearings held and 65,335 pending, across 1,895 polling stations. The notices come to 38.5 for every 100 forms digitised.
bbs-03: The same note gives the district's roll on 9 October 2026 as 10,89,133, a net rise of 2,377 from the draft that counts new voters as well as anyone put back. It counts 41,885 Form 6, 384 Form 6A, 2,245 Form 7 and 63,040 Form 8 applications received in the district from 16 June to 8 October. The note encloses the Chief Electoral Officer's letter of 1 October 2026, which noted bulk Form 7 applications before Electoral Registration Officers that were alleged to be false and directed action under section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
bbs-05: Deccan Herald printed on 6 August 2026, two weeks before the draft, the list by constituency of electors flagged as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate that the Chief Electoral Officer had put online for Bengaluru. Among B.B.M.P (South)'s seats Bommanahalli had 2,74,889 flagged, 56.68 per cent of its electors and the highest share in the city, followed by Vijayanagar at 53.18 per cent and B.T.M Layout at 53.00 per cent. Officials said no name had yet been deleted. The seven seats' figures add to more than the 10,58,028 left off at the draft, so they changed before it.
bbs-07: ThePrint reported on 28 August 2026 that the districts with the most names left off also had the most electors with no mapping to the 2002 roll. The Chief Electoral Officer's own annexure of 24 August gives B.B.M.P (South) 3,04,948 such electors, 28.1 per cent, against at most 5.69 per cent, in Kodagu, in any district outside Bengaluru. ThePrint put that range lower, at 0.03 to 3.3 per cent.
bbs-08: The Hindu reported on 20 September 2026 that Bommanahalli, a B.B.M.P (South) seat, had the highest share left off at the draft in Bengaluru, 54 per cent and more than 2.65 lakh names, nearly 11 times its 2023 winning margin of 24,215. It reported that shifted and absent together were 95 per cent of them, 50.34 per cent shifted and 45.38 per cent absent. The paper does not say where its seat figures come from, and the Chief Electoral Officer has published no table by seat.
bbs-09: Deccan Herald reported on 6 October 2026 that Jayanagar police had registered a case against BJP booth-level agents for filing Form 7 applications to delete 5,698 voters in Jayanagar, a B.B.M.P (South) seat, on a complaint by a former Congress MLA. Jayanagar's BJP MLA replied that 12,000 names in the seat should be removed as duplicate, shifted or dead, said the BJP had complained of 7,650 duplicates on 23 September, and said party workers had gone to court to quash the FIR. No reply from the Commission or the Electoral Registration Officer was reported. The 5,698 is the number of voters the complaint says those Form 7s sought to delete in one seat. The Chief Electoral Officer's 2,245 is the count of Form 7 applications received in the whole district from 16 June to 8 October. No source found reconciles the two.
bbs-04: Deccan Herald reported on 12 October 2026 that B.B.M.P (South) had 4,18,214 notices and that 4,162 electors had been rejected out of 3,87,667 hearings held. A senior official the paper did not name, speaking of the state, said rejections were mostly for failure to submit documents and that a rejected elector could appeal to the District Election Officer or apply again on Form 6. The paper reported that physical hearings were suspended on 26 September and replaced with house visits by booth-level officers.
bbs-06: The Greater Bengaluru Authority, which runs the elections in the city, asked the recognised parties in a press statement reported by Deccan Herald on 6 August 2026 to check the details and counts in the flagged list and to give any observations to the Electoral Registration Officers. The statement was for the whole city.

not_found: Any official table for Karnataka by assembly seat. The Chief Electoral Officer published the revision by election district only, so every seat figure here is a press figure, and the papers' figures differ in places.
Any statement by B.B.M.P (South)'s District Election Officer or the Greater Bengaluru Authority on why the district had the state's largest share left off.
Any split by sex of the names left off in B.B.M.P (South). The roll before the revision is published as a total only.
Any official count of names deleted in B.B.M.P (South) after a hearing. The 4,162 rejections are a press figure.
Any outcome of the Jayanagar FIR or of the petition to quash it.
The text of a report of the Chief Electoral Officer, which appeared only on Facebook, saying no voter was deleted on one ground alone.
Anything after the hearings. Karnataka's final roll is due on 27 October 2026.

cases.title: Lakhimpur, Assam
cases.intro: Lakhimpur is an assembly constituency in Assam's Lakhimpur district. Its roll fell further from the draft to the final roll of Assam's Special Revision, which differs from the SIR held elsewhere, than that of any other of the state's 126 seats.

lkp-01: The Chief Electoral Officer's table of the draft of 27 December 2025 gives Lakhimpur 210 polling stations and 1,73,362 electors, 85,283 men, 88,078 women and 1 third gender.
lkp-02: The Chief Electoral Officer's table of the final roll of 10 February 2026 gives Lakhimpur 1,63,526 electors, 81,120 men, 82,402 women and 4 third gender. That is a net fall of 9,836 from the draft, which the table does not split into names added and names deleted. The count of women fell by 5,676, which is 57.7 per cent of the net fall, against women's 50.8 per cent of the draft.
lkp-03: The final roll of the previous summary revision, of 8 February 2024, gave Lakhimpur 1,65,991 electors. The draft of the Special Revision was 7,371 above it, and the final roll of 2026 ended 2,465 below it. Two years of ordinary changes lie between the 2024 roll and the draft.
lkp-04: Lakhimpur district's five seats went from 8,64,002 electors on the draft to 8,43,004 on the final roll, a net fall of 20,998, or 24.3 for every 1,000. Lakhimpur seat's net fall of 9,836 is the largest of the five and 47 per cent of the district's.
lkp-06: The Indian Express reported on 28 January 2026 that during the claims and objections period the district administrations of Nagaon, Lakhimpur and Goalpara issued notices warning that one person filing objections against many voters was not a valid practice, and that action would follow against false, misleading or vexatious objections. The report was about the district, and the notice itself was not found.
lkp-05: The Times of India reported on 12 February 2026, from data it said it had accessed exclusively, that Lakhimpur district's roll fell about 2.4 per cent from the draft to the final roll, among the largest falls in the state with Cachar and Kamrup Metro. The paper called the fall deletions. It is net of names added.
lkp-07: Assam's Chief Electoral Officer told The Indian Express on 12 February 2026 that the final additions and deletions across the state were close to what booth-level officers found in their house visits. He said bulk Form 7 applications found invalid were summarily dismissed and not counted as applications received, and that the number dismissed was not counted. The paper reported, from his office's data, 12.97 lakh Form 7 applications received in the state, 10.63 lakh accepted, 1.9 lakh rejected and 43,536 pending. None of this was about Lakhimpur seat in particular.

not_found: Any count for Lakhimpur seat of names added and names deleted after the draft. The Chief Electoral Officer's tables give net rolls only, so the fall of 9,836 cannot be split.

Any count for Lakhimpur seat of Form 7 objections, notices or hearings. The Chief Electoral Officer's page of claims and objections by seat lists applicants by name, and the site publishes counts only.
Any statement by Lakhimpur's District Election Officer or the seat's Electoral Registration Officer on the fall.
The district administration's notice on multiple objections, in its original form.
Any court case, FIR or protest about the revision in Lakhimpur seat alone.
The 2026 Assembly result for Lakhimpur, so the fall has not been set against the winning margin.
Any report in Assamese about Lakhimpur seat in particular.
